Finding it empty, he thought to himself: "Alas! How has the wealth I earned with such difficulty been lost so easily? Being thus impoverished, how shall I show my face to my wife or my friends?" Having decided this, he went again to Vardhamanapura. There, having earned five hundred gold pieces in just a year, he set out for his home again by a different path.

As the sun was setting, he arrived at that same banyan tree. "Alas, what misery! Why has this ill-fated man started such a thing? The same demon in the form of a banyan tree has appeared again," he thought. While thinking this and pretending to be asleep, he saw those same two men on its branches. One of them said, "O Creator, why did you give five hundred gold pieces to this Somilaka? Do you not know that he has nothing beyond food and clothing?" The other replied, "O Karma, I must give to those who are industrious. The outcome depends upon the recipient. Why do you blame me?" Upon hearing this, as soon as Somilaka searched for the pouch, he saw that it was empty. Then, filled with supreme detachment, he thought: "Alas, what is the point of living for me without wealth? Therefore, I shall tie myself to this banyan tree and give up my life."

Having decided this, he fashioned a rope from kusha grass, placed the noose around his neck, and reached for the branch. Just as he was about to cast himself off, a person in the sky said this: "O Somilaka, do not commit such a rash act!
